# A clone of the engine does not say how to give an agent the Neural Link

## Context

A contributor cloned `neomjs/neo` to try 14.0 features on `dev` and asked the operator how to give their coding agent the Neural Link. The engine repository does not say. App workspaces get it from `npx neo-app`: create-app writes `.mcp.json` with `{"neural-link": {"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "neo-neural-link"]}}` (`neomjs/create-app:tasks/createAgentLayer.mjs:113`), and `neo-neural-link@1.0.0` is on npm (bin `ai/mcp/server/neural-link/standalone.mjs`, published 2026-10-26).

## The Problem

- `CONTRIBUTING.md:185` promises "Your agent needs nothing beyond the clone above", yet the clone section (`:14` to `:25`) registers no MCP server.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md:194` names the server by a path in the Brain repository (`neo-agent-brain:ai/mcp/server/neural-link/`), not by the npm package a cloner can run.
- `.github/AI_QUICK_START.md` starts the Neural Link from a Brain checkout and never names `neo-neural-link`. It also says Claude Desktop and Claude Code share one MCP configuration file, which `.claude/claude_desktop_config.example.json` contradicts: Claude Code reads `.mcp.json`.
- The app side is already on: `examples/button/base`, several grid examples and `apps/ai/neural-link` set `useAiClient: true`, and `neuralLinkUrl` defaults to `ws://127.0.0.1:8081` (`src/DefaultConfig.mjs:193`). Only the agent side is missing.

## The Architectural Reality

- Server: `neo-neural-link` on npm, built from `neo-agent-brain:ai/mcp/server/neural-link/`; its Bridge listens on 127.0.0.1:8081.
- App side: `Neo.config.useAiClient` (default `false`, `src/DefaultConfig.mjs:295`) and `neuralLinkUrl`.
- Precedent: create-app's agent layer writes Claude Code's `.mcp.json` and Codex's `.codex/config.toml`.
- Design authority: `CONTRIBUTING.md:185`, "Your agent needs nothing beyond the clone above". The clone section owns that promise, and today it does not hold for the Neural Link.

## The Fix

1. `CONTRIBUTING.md`, "Set up the engine from a clone": a short step that gives the agent the Neural Link. It names the `.mcp.json` entry for Claude Code and the `[mcp_servers.neural-link]` entry for Codex (both `npx -y neo-neural-link`), the example to open after `npm run server-start`, and how to switch `useAiClient` on for any other app.
2. `CONTRIBUTING.md:194` names the npm package and links that step.
3. `.github/AI_QUICK_START.md`: the Neural Link starts from the npm package, and the shared-configuration sentence is corrected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A fresh clone of `dev`, following only `CONTRIBUTING.md`, connects Claude Code to a running example through `npx -y neo-neural-link`, and one Neural Link tool call answers with that app's component tree. The pull request shows the commands and the answer.
- [ ] The same for Codex, or the pull request names why it could not be measured.
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md:194` and `.github/AI_QUICK_START.md` name `neo-neural-link`, and neither sends a cloner to a Brain checkout.
- [ ] No sentence claims that Claude Desktop and Claude Code share one MCP configuration file.

## Out of Scope

- A command that writes the harness configuration for a clone, shared with create-app's agent layer. It is worth building once the documented step is measured.
- What `npm install` writes into `AGENTS.md` for a cloner (a survey reports maintainer-only Memory Core rules; it gets its own ticket after verification).
- Publishing a newer `neo-neural-link`. If 1.0.0 does not work with `dev`, the first AC files that as a Brain ticket.
